note: Live Activity cases: the region roots, their node caps, and the ContentState that travels in the push. The 4 KB cap is Apple's; ours is 3.5 KB, and the server, BotsLiveActivity.parse() and the JS activity plan must all land on the same answer for the same input. Activity.request and update above 4 KB fail SILENTLY, which is why this is measured three times rather than trusted once.

designCases.why: Every activity root at once. A region a design does not hold falls back on its own to today's hand-drawn region, so a partial design is normal, not an error.
Only the lock banner is redesigned. Every island region keeps today's hand-drawn view, region by region.
An activity region has no Grid: the regions are small and the layout must stay cheap to re-render on every push.
On an activity an Each is 3 copies at most, whatever the design asks for: more would not fit a region and would cost push bytes for nothing.
The minimal region is 3 nodes; compact is 6; each island region is 20; the lock banner is 50. The generator repeats a Text 6 times in minimal.

One art key can be used in BOTH the island and the banner, so the cap is applied per region at load: island at most 135 px, lock at most 252 px. Without that, an island would decode a banner-sized image inside the extension's ~30 MB.

stateCases.why: A body from today's server, with none of the new fields. The decode is lenient and every new field is optional, so an old push must still render on a new build.

THE T0 BUG. The server already sends `private` and `failed` (activity.ts), and today's ContentState CodingKeys omits them, so iOS drops both. Both copies of BotsAtWorkAttributes must decode them, inside the BEGIN/END markers, and a CI script diffs the marked region in both files.
The other half of the same bug: a job that ended with a problem. `failed` tells the view to draw the result as a problem, not a success.

state.result: Stopped: the tests did not pass

stateCases.why: The push names a design that is ALREADY on the phone and carries only data. The 4 KB cap limits the data, never the design: the design waits in the App Group and the Activity's views read it from there (FlowActivity.swift already reads that group).
A design named by a push that the phone does not hold draws today's view, every region. The app refetches the catalog on its next run; nothing is ever downloaded during a render.
vars is 12 keys, a key 24 characters, a value 120. It is the one way a future design binds new data without another change to the frozen struct, so it is clamped rather than refused.
